clue.text: Reserve bank works here

definitions.note: literary works stand on it, so 'works here' describes the place they are kept

parts.note: to reserve a table or seat is to book it
a shelf is a bank or ledge, as in a sandbank or continental shelf

explanation.surface: A reserve bank's staff carry out their duties in this building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve bank' reads as a central bank; split, it is two charade pieces, and 'works' is books, not labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Books, the written works, are kept on a shelf, so this phrase is a cryptic pointer to that furniture.

clue.text: Stop eating firm meat

indicators.note: one word eating another takes it into its middle, so the firm goes inside the stop

parts.note: to stop something is to ban it
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Someone is told to quit eating a tough cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is cured pork, a familiar kind of meat.

clue.text: Slow absorption I found in very big Scottish bog

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

indicators.note: a letter found in a word sits inside it, so I goes into the bog

parts.note: in Scotland and northern England a moss is a peat bog

explanation.surface: Water seeps slowly into a huge Scottish peat bog where I am standing.
explanation.walkthrough: MOSS for a bog is a Scottish and northern English usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is the gradual passage of a liquid through a membrane, a slow soaking-in.

clue.text: Sheepish journalist follows fake eatery up

indicators.note: the journalist follows, so that piece comes last

parts.note: a sham is a fake

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a cafe is a small eatery
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: An embarrassed reporter trails after a bogus restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamefaced and sheepish both describe someone looking embarrassed or guilty.

clue.text: It takes ages to manage rearing horse

indicators.note: in a down entry rearing means rising up, so the word for managing is read upwards

parts.note: to cope is to manage
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: Getting a horse to rear up seems to take forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearing' turns COPE into EPOC. Horse is drug slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long era of history or geology, a span lasting ages.

clue.text: Eve welcoming half-cut Adam in for starters

indicators.note: a word welcoming another takes it inside

parts.note: firstly means to begin with, for starters

indicators.note: only half of the name is kept, the first two of its four letters

explanation.surface: Eve takes in a tipsy Adam, beginning their story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' looks like slang for drunk, but here it halves the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve was the first woman in Genesis, so she is wryly called the first lady.

clue.text: Add space for printer's family emblem

parts.note: to tot up is to add
an em is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: A typesetter is told to add a gap for a family crest.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or animal adopted as the emblem of a clan or family.

clue.text: One-piece garment not new in Friendly Islands

indicators.note: not new means the letter for new is left out

parts.note: Captain Cook named Tonga the Friendly Islands

explanation.surface: An old style of single garment is worn on a Pacific island chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman toga was a single draped piece of cloth wrapped around the body.

clue.text: They get beaten up in a mine skirting motorway

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upward
the mine skirts, going round the motorway

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Miners near a motorway get beaten up underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten up' reads as an assault; 'beaten' belongs to the definition and 'up' reverses the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are kettledrums, so they are struck with sticks in an orchestra.

clue.text: In Paris, my old box contains top-class speech

parts.note: mon is French for my

indicators.note: the box contains the letter for top-class inside it

parts.note: a loge is a box in a theatre
U means upper-class, so top-class

explanation.surface: A French speaker's old theatre box holds a grand oration.
explanation.walkthrough: LOGE is the French word for a theatre box, also used in English.
explanation.definitionFit: A monologue is a long speech by one person.

clue.text: Company accepting blame replaced instrument

indicators.note: the company accepts the rearranged letters into its middle
the letters are replaced in a new order

explanation.surface: A firm takes the blame for swapping out a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' looks like swapped for another, but means placed again in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A cembalo is a harpsichord, a keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Troops short of time prescribed treatment

indicators.note: short of time means lacking the letter for time

parts.note: a regiment is a body of troops

explanation.surface: Soldiers too busy for anything follow a doctor's course of treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a set course of diet, exercise or medicine laid down by a doctor.

clue.text: NHS uses tin complex as service accommodation

indicators.note: complex as an adjective means intricate or tangled, signalling a jumbled arrangement

explanation.surface: The health service uses a tin-roofed complex to house staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' rearranges NHS USES TIN. The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Nissen huts are curved corrugated-iron shelters used to house military personnel.

clue.text: Dog that always investigates leather leads

indicators.note: the leads of the words are their front letters, which are taken

explanation.surface: A dog that sniffs out leather on its lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' looks like dog leads, but it signals the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow closely, which is also to tail them.

clue.text: Bird flu wigeon spread around area

indicators.note: the jumble is placed around the letter for area
the letters are spread about into a new order

explanation.surface: Avian flu carried by a wigeon spreads through a region.
explanation.walkthrough: The wigeon is a duck, a fitting bird for the surface, but only its letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: The guinea fowl is a speckled African game bird.

clue.text: View street through fences

indicators.note: to fence something is to enclose it, so one word is enclosed by the other

parts.note: via means by way of, through

explanation.surface: Someone peers down a road through a line of fences.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a pleasing prospect or outlook, a view.

clue.text: Call recorder perhaps active man picked up

parts.note: active is a voice of the verb in grammar

indicators.note: something picked up is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: A lively man takes the telephone receiver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns MALE into its sound-alike MAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Voicemail stores telephone messages, one example of a device recording calls.

clue.text: Not entertaining girl, American, when visiting China

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

indicators.note: the American is visiting, so goes inside the china

parts.note: Ming is fine porcelain of the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: A dull girl travels with an American around China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' reads as the country; it is porcelain, MING.
explanation.definitionFit: Unamusing means failing to entertain, dull.

clue.text: Blue Berets loved defending northern plain

parts.note: UN peacekeepers wear blue berets

indicators.note: the word for loved surrounds and protects the northern letter

parts.note: adored means loved

explanation.surface: Popular UN peacekeepers guard a northern plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like flat land but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Unadorned means without decoration, which is plain.

clue.text: Planned route I go around in time

indicators.note: the attempt goes around the following pieces

parts.note: to have a go is to have a try
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A traveller commits to a plan of travel to finish in time.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerary is a planned journey route.

clue.text: Understanding paper conservationists import pine

parts.note: the i is a British national newspaper

indicators.note: to import is to bring in, so the yearning goes inside the conservationists

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, a UK heritage conservation body
to pine is to sigh or yearn

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports on conservationists importing pine timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' reads as the tree but is the verb, to sigh.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep perception of something, understanding.

clue.text: Grand book stolen from dope?

indicators.note: a thing stolen from another is taken out of it

parts.note: to nobble a racehorse is to drug or dope it

explanation.surface: A book has been stolen from a drug dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble means stately or imposing, grand.

clue.text: Proud words misled Liberal

indicators.note: the letters are led astray into another order

explanation.surface: Boastful rhetoric deceived a Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proud' means standing out from a surface: braille's dots are raised.
explanation.definitionFit: Braille is writing for blind readers in raised dots, words that stand proud of the page.

clue.text: Queen avoids sickly piece of cake

indicators.note: the queen avoids the word, so her letters are removed

parts.note: queasy means feeling sick

explanation.surface: The monarch declines a slice of cake that makes her ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy and a piece of cake both mean simple to do, the second an idiom.

clue.text: Saxophonist's first recently to hide fitting round mouthpiece?

indicators.note: the first letter of the musician's name is taken
the phrase for recently hides the fitting word inside

parts.note: of late means recently

indicators.note: turned round means read backwards

parts.note: apt means fitting

explanation.surface: A saxophonist recently fitted a new mouthpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mouthpiece' suggests the reed fitting of a sax; the question mark flags a piece of the mouth itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft palate is part of the roof of the mouth, playfully a piece of the mouth.

clue.text: Unionists embracing Northern Irish outfit

indicators.note: the unionists embrace the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: the TUC is the Trades Union Congress, Britain's federation of trade unions
NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Unionists wear traditional Northern Irish costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unionists' suggests Northern Irish politics; here it means trade unionists.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a loose garment, an item of outfit or uniform.

clue.text: Follow guarantee, ignoring Republican

indicators.note: ignoring the Republican means leaving its letter out

parts.note: to ensure is to guarantee

explanation.surface: A political pledge is followed while ignoring the Republicans.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on as a result.

clue.text: Gentle touch of some gracious Sikh in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the letters are read backwards
some of these words means a run of their letters is taken

explanation.surface: A kindly Sikh pensioner offers a soft touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss is a light touch of the lips.

clue.text: Church member mislays clubs belonging to ancient invaders?

indicators.note: the church member mislays, so loses, a letter

parts.note: an Anglican is a member of the Church of England
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

explanation.surface: A churchgoer loses their golf clubs to invaders.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angles were Germanic invaders of Britain, and Anglian describes things of theirs.

clue.text: Top soprano initially improvises

parts.note: noodle is slang for the head, the top of the body

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A leading soprano ad-libs on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like a description of the soprano but is a noun, the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To noodle is to play music in a casual, improvised way.

clue.text: Many adopting universal yoga position

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the universal letter goes inside

parts.note: lots means many
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Many people take up a universal yoga pose.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a cross-legged seated posture in yoga.

clue.text: Remove housing officer, revealing clothing

indicators.note: the word for remove houses the officer inside it

parts.note: to delete is to remove
COL is the abbreviation for colonel, an officer

explanation.surface: An officer is evicted from his lodgings and exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Decollete describes a low-cut neckline, clothing that shows the neck and shoulders.
